paper_title: MathOdyssey Benchmarking Mathematical Problem-Solving Skills in Large   Language Models Using Odyssey Math Data
caption: Mathematical problems across educational levels. We curate and categorize problems by difficulty and subject area.
model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of mathematical problems categorized by subject area and educational level, as part of the MathOdyssey benchmark. It displays ten distinct segments, each representing a specific subject and its corresponding difficulty level, with associated percentages and counts in parentheses. The largest segment is **Algebra – Olympiad-level** at 21.19% (82 problems), followed by **Algebra – High School** at 17.83% (69), and **Pre-Calculus – High School** at 14.21% (55). Other notable segments include **Combinatorics – Olympiad-level** at 9.56% (37), **Geometry – Olympiad-level** at 6.46% (25), and **Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level** at 6.46% (25). Smaller segments represent **Calculus and Analysis – University-level** (6.20%, 24), **Probability – University-level** (5.43%, 21), **Statistics – University-level** (4.39%, 17), and **Geometry – High School** (3.62%, 14). The chart uses distinct colors for each category and includes percentage labels and problem counts directly on or near each slice, with lines connecting the labels to their respective segments. The segments are arranged in a clockwise order, roughly descending by size, starting from the largest (Algebra – Olympiad-level) and moving toward the smallest (Geometry – High School).
